4. 5. Architecture boundaries — pass. Selector classifies/executes support decisions without authoring models. CLI discovery retains factual/read-only behavior. 6. Compatibility — pass for the approved breaking boundary. Historical Skill archive mappings, old examples prefix, generic flat/relocation model aliases, record schema versions and architecture/adr/other location kinds remain unchanged. Existing customer material remains readable source authority; installation or old templates do not authorize conversion or restore retired output support. Deleted bytes are bound to the baseline identities below and remain Git-recoverable.

7. Security/privacy — pass. Unsupported private input is never read and fixture/source trees remain unchanged; model diagnostics hash offending values rather than disclosing raw content. Existing model/reference tests retain symlink/escape rejection, path containment and projection no-outside-mutation. workflow-context withdrawal rejects visibly with no candidate discovery and preserves config/customer bytes. No new network action, permission expansion, record rewrite or publication is introduced.

8. Derived artifact currency — pass within observed local evidence. Canonical compact-core and all eight projections match; exact closed manifest removes two exclusive resources. Independent feature-retirement-tg-method observed real generated Codex/Claude archives (136 members each), local CLI installations and all 87 inspected files per target, with every resource byte matching canonical and retired methods absent. Packaging native 95 cases provides actual archive/packed CLI installation checks. No claim about hosted installations or public registry currency.
